validity.researcher_notes: Existence, classification, ownership, route, and every spec value are independently confirmed; no duplicate, misclassification, or fabricated value found. UGI Sunbury, LLC is a real FERC/NGA-jurisdictional interstate natural gas pipeline (Docket No. CP15-525-000; PF15-9-000): the FERC Federal Register notice of application (2015-17810, 80 FR 43080-43081, filed July 1, 2015) states the project as 'new interstate natural gas pipeline facilities (Sunbury Pipeline Project)... approximately 34.4 miles of 20-inch-diameter pipeline in Snyder, Union, Northumberland, Montour, and Lycoming Counties, Pennsylvania,' running 'generally north to south' from an interconnection with Transcontinental Gas Pipeline Company and the MARC I Pipeline at its northern (Lycoming County) end to the 'Hummel Station Generating Facility at the existing site of the coal-fired Sunbury Generating Facility in Snyder County, Pennsylvania' at its southern end, 'designed to add an additional 200,000 Dth/d of new pipeline capacity,' with 'the estimated cost of the Project... $178,243,345.' Independently, an unrelated secondary publisher (hydrocarbons-technology.com/GlobalData, a project profile not sourced from GEM) restates the same facts from the built/operating side: 'Sunbury Pipeline is a 35mi (56km) long pipeline owned and operated by UGI Energy Services, through its subsidiary UGI Sunbury'; 'The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) granted a certificate of public convenience and necessity to UGI Sunbury for the pipeline's construction in May 2016'; 'The new pipeline was commissioned in early 2017'; 'The 20in-diameter steel pipeline is designed to deliver up to 200,000 decatherms (Dth) of natural gas per day'; and the identical county-by-county route (Lycoming -> Montour, Northumberland, Union -> Hummel Station near Shamokin Dam, Snyder County). A trade-press item (electricenergyonline.com, 'Sunbury Pipeline Receives FERC Approval,' May 3, 2016) independently corroborates the FERC certificate date and identifies 'UGI Sunbury, LLC, a subsidiary of UGI Energy Services, LLC' as the certificate holder -- matching Operator=UGI Sunbury LLC and Owner1=UGI Energy (i.e. UGI Energy Services) 100%. The operator's own current site (sunburypipeline.com) states: 'The Sunbury Pipeline, originated in 2017, is a federally-regulated 35-mile, 20-inch pipeline with related facilities in Snyder, Union, Northumberland, Montour and Lycoming Counties, Pennsylvania... owned and operated by a subsidiary of UGI Energy Services... interconnects to... Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company ('Transco'), Marc I Pipeline ('Marc I'), Hummel Station... delivers low-cost Marcellus natural gas.' SPEC CHECKS: Length=35.00mi -- the FERC application's pre-construction estimate was 34.4mi; the as-built figure in both the operator site and hydrocarbons-technology is 35mi -- a normal proposed-vs-built rounding difference (1.7%), not a material disagreement, so LengthKnown=35.00 stands unchanged. Diameter=20in -- exact match, 3 independent sources (FERC, hydrocarbons-technology, operator site). Capacity=200.00 MMcf/d -- FERC's 200,000 Dth/d and hydrocarbons-technology's identical 200,000 Dth/d figure are the standard Dth<->Mcf near-equivalence (~1.03 MMBtu/Mcf for pipeline-quality gas), so 200 MMcf/d is a good match, not a conversion error. SegmentCost=178,000,000.00 USD -- matches the FERC notice's precise estimate of $178,243,345 (rounds to $178M; 0.14% difference, clearly the same figure). ConstructionYear/Month=2016/5 and StartYear1=2017 -- both independently corroborated (FERC certificate approval + construction start May 2016 per hydrocarbons-technology and electricenergyonline; commissioning/origination in 2017 per hydrocarbons-technology and the operator site). CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is correct -- this is an NGA Section 7(c) interstate transmission certificate holder, not a gathering/distribution line. DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against the full 46-row Appalachian-basin roster; no other row's name, route, or operator overlaps with Sunbury (unique corridor Lycoming->Snyder County, PA; unique operator UGI Sunbury LLC) -- no merge/relabel candidate. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='UGI Energy' at 100% matches 'UGI Energy Services, LLC' (the parent that owns UGI Sunbury, LLC 100%) per the electricenergyonline and hydrocarbons-technology sources -- the sheet's shortened form is consistent with the full legal name, not a different entity. FuelSource='Marcellus Shale' is corroborated only by the operator's own site ('delivers low-cost Marcellus natural gas') -- I searched the FERC notice, hydrocarbons-technology, electricenergyonline and pgjonline for a second, non-operator confirmation of the gas source and found none (the FERC notice describes route/capacity/cost but never names a producing basin); this is plausible on its face (Central PA is within the Marcellus play, and the pipeline interconnects with the Marc I Pipeline, itself named for the Marcellus) but should be treated as medium tier, single-source, until a second source is found. WIKI CITATION POOL: opened/tested 10 of the 12 harvested citations -- sunburypipeline.com (live, used), sunburypipeline.com/overview/ (confirmed HTTP 404 -- the site was restructured to a single homepage; the live homepage above covers the same content so nothing is lost), electricenergyonline.com (live, used), federalregister.gov (live, used -- this is the standout find, not previously staged), pgjonline.com (live but paywalled beyond the same May-2016-approval headline, not independently useful beyond corroborating the date), hydrocarbons-technology.com (live, used, most detailed), ugies.com (live but generic UGI Energy Services homepage, does not name Sunbury specifically -- not usable as a Sunbury ref), eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php (live but a generic data-portal landing page, does not name Sunbury -- a navigation surface, not a document), fractracker.org's national map article (live but does not name Sunbury specifically in the fetched text). Not opened: rbnenergy.com/node/5296 (HTTP 403, blocked -- access failure, not a deletion; not needed given the sourcing already assembled) and the spglobal.com Insight Weekly blog post (HTTP 403, blocked). ijglobal.com's 'Asset Data' citation is a paywalled search-projects page (redirects to a login/search surface), not a citable document.

verifications.note: 'Take notice that on July 1, 2015, UGI Sunbury, LLC (Sunbury)... filed an application pursuant to section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act... requesting: (i) A certificate authorizing Sunbury to construct, own, and operate new interstate natural gas pipeline facilities (Sunbury Pipeline Project)...' -- the NGA Section 7(c) certificate application is the formal proposal filing.

fills.researcher_notes: The July 1, 2015 filing date is the formal certificate-application date and is the standard basis for ProposalYear/Month. Single source (govt regulatory filing) -- searched hydrocarbons-technology.com, sunburypipeline.com, electricenergyonline.com, and pgjonline.com for a second, independent statement of the original application/filing date; all four discuss only the later May-2016 certificate-grant/construction-start and 2017 in-service milestones, not the 2015 filing date itself, so no second source was found for this specific fact. FERC's own docket record also notes a Dec. 30, 2014 pre-filing (Docket PF15-9-000) that preceded the formal application, but that is the same origin (FERC), not an independent second source, and pre-filing activity is not itself a proposal/application date, so it was not used.

No operating-pressure/MAOP figure was found in any source read: the FERC Federal Register notice of application states length/diameter/capacity/cost/route but no pressure; hydrocarbons-technology.com's project profile, the operator's own site, and electricenergyonline.com's approval notice likewise omit it. A PHMSA NPMS or annual-report pull, or the FERC docket's actual certificate order/tariff (behind eLibrary, not fetched in this pass), would be the next place to look for MAOP. Left UNRESOLVED rather than guessing.

summary: P0291 Sunbury Pipeline confirmed (caveat): real, correctly classified, no duplicate -- every spec (35mi/20in/200MMcf-d/2016 construction/2017 in-service/$178M cost) independently corroborated by a FERC Federal Register notice (Docket CP15-525) newly found beyond the wiki's citation pool, plus hydrocarbons-technology.com and the operator's own site; FuelSource=Marcellus Shale is single-sourced (operator only). Filled ProposalYear/Month=2015/7 (FERC filing date, medium tier, single source). Pressure remains UNRESOLVED -- no source states an MAOP/operating pressure.
